title: Parameter exploration — effect of MAX_WORDS/ROUNDS/model on debate quality + cost (Epic 14, issue #100)
prompt:
Run a small parameter sweep over MAX_WORDS/ROUNDS/model and report the effect on debate quality and cost.

Follow repo standards: TDD (write the failing test first, then code); max 150 lines per code file (split, don't compress); ruff = 0 violations + mypy clean; no hard-coded values (read from config); every external API call goes through the API gatekeeper (Epic 13); log via the LOG package; keep coverage >= 85%. Read docs/PRD.md and the relevant docs/prds/*.md before starting.

usage.summary: Read PRD §9 (research) + §10 (cost-vs-scale), the 14.1/14.2 research package, the Epic-15 pricing code + config/model_prices.json, and the 14.3 notebook/viz conventions. TDD red-first params test; built a pure parameter-exploration module reusing the existing aggregation + pricing (no re-implementation); added a parameter-exploration section to the notebook; full gate suite. NO new paid debates — cost-free, derived from the 4 existing runs + the validated cost model + the config price table.

note: COST CONSTRAINT HONOURED: ran ZERO new real/paid debates. The exploration is built entirely from (1) the 4 committed runs (already span ROUNDS in {3,4,10}, MAX_WORDS in {120,150}), (2) the validated PRD §10 cost model (output ~linear in ROUNDS*MAX_WORDS, input ~quadratic in ROUNDS from context replay), and (3) the config price table config/model_prices.json. NEW MODULE: packages/core/src/agent_debate/core/research/params.py (~69 code lines, under 150 cap), pure functions reusing the 14.1 RunSummary rows + Epic-15 compute_cost/PriceTable (adds NO pricing logic): empirical_points (observed rounds->tokens/cost/latency, sorted), TokenModel + fit_token_model (scales the §10 model from the richest observed run via a documented DEFAULT_OUTPUT_FRACTION=0.2 input/output split constant — not a price), project_grid (rounds x max_words grid priced per the table, input/output split explicit), model_choice_table (same nominal usage priced under several models). No hard-coded prices/paths: prices come solely from the injected/loaded PriceTable; rounds/max_words/model read from settings in the notebook. TDD RED-FIRST: NEW packages/core/tests/test_research_params.py (9 tests, synthetic fixtures + a test-injected PriceTable): empirical_points sorted/empty, fit empty->None, fit recovers scale, project_grid doubling-rounds ~doubles output cost (1.8-2.2x), doubling max_words ~doubles output cost, input grows faster than output in rounds, model_choice prices same usage differently (cheap<mid<dear) with an exact 2.0 assertion, empty models. Watched the import fail (RED) then GREEN. 100% coverage on params.py. NOTEBOOK: added a §6 Parameter exploration section to notebooks/analysis.ipynb (markdown intro stating the cost-free 3-source method + honest n=4 caveat; 6a projected cost grid code cell; 6b model-choice code cell; interpretation markdown connecting to quality+cost — more rounds=more rebuttal depth but super-linear cost, higher max_words=longer messages/higher per-turn output tokens, Opus controller dearer per token than Sonnet debaters, Haiku the cheap trade-off). Executed end-to-end against the real runs to confirm it runs clean (Sonnet 10r/150w=$1.855, Haiku=$0.618, Opus=$9.275; 5r/120w=$0.577 ~= the 4x saving §10 predicts); committed with code-cell outputs CLEARED per the notebook convention (the 14.2 smoke test forbids text/stream outputs — kept green). GATES GREEN: uv sync clean; ruff check . = All checks passed; ruff format --check . = 247 files already formatted; mypy = Success 244 source files; pytest --cov = 858 passed, 99.24% total (params.py 100%) >= 85%; check_line_limit.py passed; secret_scan only flags the real local gitignored .env (documented pre-existing, never committed). PRE-EXISTING failures unchanged (6 failed + 2 errors, identical to clean main): branch-protection Unix perms x2, live-tree secret scan/hygiene x2 (real .env), Windows missing-file path-regex x2 (test_price_table + test_rate_limit_config), long-topic parametrized teardown errors x2 — NO new failures.
